questions.question: Write a brief description of First Come First Serve CPU Scheduling / Algorithm.
questions.solution_html:
• FCFS is the simplest scheduling method where processes are executed in the order they
  • arrive in the ready queue. It is non-preemptive and can lead to the “convoy effect.” Example
  • If processes arrive in order of burst time 10, 5, 2, the average waiting time can be high due
  • to long jobs at the front.
  • Definition -(2 marks)
  • Explanation of FCFS Algorithm -(5 marks)
  • Advantages and Limitations-(3marks)
  • Total=(10 marks)

questions.question: Apply the concept of virtual memory to explain how a 32-bit logical / address space can be mapped onto a smaller physical memory using paging.
questions.solution_html:
• Apply the Concept of Virtual Memory to explain how a 32-bit Logical Address Space can
  • be mapped onto a Smaller Physical Memory using Paging.
  • Virtual memory allows processes to use more memory than physically available by storing
  • inactive pages on disk. A 32-bit address can reference 4 GB of virtual space, which is
  • divided into pages mapped dynamically to physical frames using a page table.
  • Concept and Definition of virtual memory- (2marks)
  • Explanation of paging mechanism-(3 marks)
  • Diagram/Address-mapping example -(3 marks)
  • Benefits and practical uses- (2marks)
  • Total=(10 marks)

questions.question: Differentiate between programmed I/O, interrupt-driven I/O, and DMA, / and evaluate which is most efficient in high-speed data transfer.
questions.solution_html:
• which is most efficient in High-Speed Data Transfer.
  • Programmed I/O: CPU actively waits for I/O completion.
  • Interrupt-driven I/O: Device sends an interrupt when ready, freeing CPU time.
  • DMA (Direct Memory Access): Data is transferred directly between memory and device
  • without CPU involvement.
  • Most efficient: DMA, especially for large data transfers.
  • Definition of each I/O method-(3 marks)
  • Comparative table or differences-(3 marks)
  • Evaluation of efficiency with reason-(3 marks)
  • Suitable application example-(1 mark)
  • Total=(10 marks)
  • END OF SCHEME
